- [USER] User requested the start of a script for a movie scene.
- [USER] User provided detailed background information about Arena Television and its directors, Richard Yeowart and Robert Hopkinson.
- [FACT] Arena Television was a failed outside broadcast business at the center of the UK’s “largest ever” asset-based lending fraud.
- [FACT] Richard Yeowart and Robert Hopkinson were made bankrupt after failing to respond to a High Court judgment ordering repayment of £100 million.
- [FACT] Arena Television collapsed in November 2022 and is suspected of defrauding lenders out of about £280 million.
- [FACT] Yeowart and Hopkinson were initially asked to repay £250 million.
- [FACT] A default judgment of £100 million, plus costs of £500,000, was granted by the High Court.
- [FACT] Yeowart and Hopkinson were made bankrupt in February 2023 after failing to respond to a statutory demand.
- [FACT] Arena Television was incorporated in 1988 and worked on major events including the European football championship and Glastonbury festival.
- [FACT] Yeowart ordered Arena to cease trading in November 2022 after concerns were raised about a non-existent asset linked to a loan.
- [FACT] Administrators found that Arena had borrowed against equipment that either did not exist or had already been used to secure a loan from another lender.
- [FACT] 55 lenders are owed £282 million, much of which is likely to be lost.
- [FACT] 46 lenders, owed a combined £182 million, “do not have recourse to any assets” underlying their lending.
- [FACT] Yeowart and Hopkinson were believed to be living in France before the scam was uncovered.
- [FACT] Yeowart has outright ownership in properties in the UK, France, and Spain, but the combined identified assets are worth only a small proportion of the amount owed.
- [FACT] A £1.5 million property in Barcelona owned by Yeowart is being held on trust following the judgment.
- [FACT] A worldwide freezing injunction was obtained against both directors in November 2022.
- [FACT] The Serious Fraud Office began a criminal investigation into the scandal in February 2023.
- [FACT] Two arrests were made of unnamed individuals, and three properties were searched.
- [FACT] Yeowart and Hopkinson were not arrested.
- [FACT] Yeowart used a Hong Kong entity called Sports Online to perpetrate a complex alleged fraud involving fake equipment.
- [FACT] Court filings allege that Yeowart forged labels with false serial numbers in a locked room at Arena TV’s headquarters.
